title: Imager deletes original file after an HTTP error response
summary: `indigo_server/resource/imager.html:507-519` handles xhr.onload by clicking a download link for any response and then sending AGENT_IMAGER_DELETE_FILE with the original filename. onload runs for completed HTTP404/500 responses too, and this callback does not inspect status. An ordinary expired/missing BLOB or server failure can therefore download an error body and then request deletion of the original image. This is a normal failure-handling issue; no server-security test was involved. The exact committed callback was executed in Node24.19.0 with a synthetic XMLHttpRequest status404 and Blob('BLOB not found!'), mocked DOM/blob URL, and captur Full evidence: C-05. Remediation: require a successful and complete image response before advancing/deleting, preserve the original and present an error/retry path on HTTP/transport/abort failures, and avoid relying on mutable global filename during asynchronous completion. Regression tests must show404/500/abort never enqueue deletion and successful transfer maintains the established sequence.
evidence: core-functional-review.md section C-05; exact source and ordinary functional proof retained there.
